answer: Weight the rank of the settlement graph, not headcount: sybils multiply keys, not relationships. Each epoch an identity commits the counterparties it truly paid during the voyage; a post-commitment probe tests rows for linear dependence. A farm's aliases share a few outsiders and mostly trade with each other, so a whole knoll spans one dimension: extra keys add no rank, circular self-payment nets to zero. Buying k votes needs k distinct counterparties with capital locked W epochs, all slashable if one controller surfaces. No ivory polish on a fresh key helps; an honest agent pays one bond.
